description: Which request paths may be turned into a prerendered-document or public-asset file path. The native server decides this in `is_safe_relative_path` (crates/ruvyxa_dev_server/src/static_assets.rs) and the deployed handler in `isUnsafeSegment`/`prerenderRelativePath` (packages/ruvyxa/runtime/serverless-handler.mjs). Neither can call the other, and the rule guards a path that is written as well as read, so both replay this table.
rule: A path is safe when every non-empty segment is not `.` or `..`, and contains no `/`, `\`, `:`, or control character.
note: Paths are given without a leading slash, as `is_safe_relative_path` receives them; the handler is fed the same values with a `/` prefix. The site root is deliberately absent: both callers resolve an empty path to the root document before this rule is consulted.

cases.why: decoded spaces are legal in a segment
dots inside a segment are not a `.` segment
a bare `.` segment is not a route the build emits
colon names an NTFS alternate data stream on Windows; only `a:` parsed as a drive prefix, so multi-character names slipped through
control characters never name a real file
DEL is a control character too

C1 controls are control characters too: Rust's `char::is_control()` covers U+0080-U+009F, and the JavaScript copy stopped at U+007F, so the three owners of this rule disagreed with no case here to say so
